summary: GitHub OAuth apps are self-serve. You register one in Developer settings in about 5 minutes, and any GitHub user can authorize it right away. There is no app review, no verification and no user cap. Composio also offers a managed GitHub app, so you only need your own app if you want your branding, custom scopes or separate rate limits. The biggest catch is organizations: OAuth app access restrictions are on by default for new orgs. Until an org owner approves your app, users can authorize it but it can't see that org's private repos. SAML SSO orgs add a second authorization step on top of that.

verdict.difficultyReason: Self-serve registration, no review or verification, and any GitHub user can connect immediately; only org-level approval (controlled by each customer's org owner) adds friction.

devReady.estimate: 5-15 min (0 min if you use Composio's managed app)
devReady.detail: Register an OAuth app, paste the client ID and secret into a Composio auth config, then connect your own GitHub account. There is no test-user list or dev mode: the app works for every account from the start.

productionReady.estimate: Same day. Org-owned private data depends on each org owner approving the app (minutes to days, outside your control).
productionReady.detail: GitHub doesn't review or approve OAuth apps. Personal repos and public data work for every user right away. For private resources in an org with OAuth app access restrictions (the default for new orgs), an org owner has to approve the app under Org Settings > Third-party Access > OAuth app policy. A GitHub Marketplace listing is optional and only matters for discovery or billing.

nextAction: Sign in and register an OAuth app at https://github.com/settings/applications/new. Use Authorization callback URL = https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Or skip this step and start with Composio's managed GitHub app.

accessPaths.name: Composio managed OAuth app
accessPaths.whenToUse: Prototypes, internal tools, getting started today
accessPaths.limits: The consent screen shows Composio. You get only the default scopes (repo,user,gist,notifications,project,workflow,codespace). Quota is shared with other Composio users. Triggers poll every 15 minutes at minimum. Org owners must approve Composio's app, not yours.

accessPaths.name: Your own OAuth app (personal or org-owned)
accessPaths.whenToUse: Production agent products that need their own branding, custom scopes or their own rate limits
accessPaths.limits: No user cap. Up to 10 callback URLs per app and 100 OAuth apps per owner. Each user token has the normal REST limit, typically 5,000 requests/hour. Max 10 tokens per user/app/scope combination, and 10 token creations per hour. Each org's restrictions need owner approval.

accessPaths.name: GitHub Marketplace listing (optional)
accessPaths.whenToUse: Only if you want discovery in GitHub Marketplace or GitHub billing
accessPaths.timeline: Days to weeks (GitHub reviews listings, paid plans need extra verification)
accessPaths.limits: Not needed for OAuth to work

A full URL for your product. It appears on the consent screen. No domain verification is needed.
You can upload it after registration. It shows on the consent screen.

phases.title: Register the OAuth app
phases.goal: You have a Client ID and Client Secret

steps.title: Open Developer settings > OAuth apps
steps.detail: Profile picture > Settings > Developer settings > OAuth apps > New OAuth App. The button says 'Register a new application' if this is your first app. For an org-owned app, go to Org Settings > Developer settings > OAuth apps instead.

steps.title: Fill in the form
steps.detail: Application name: your product name. It's public, so don't put internal names or URLs in it. Homepage URL: your site. Application description: optional, and users see it. Authorization callback URL: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Leave 'Enable Device Flow' unchecked.

steps.title: Decide on 'Expire user access tokens'
steps.detail: This box is checked by default for new apps. It makes access tokens last 8 hours and refresh tokens 6 months, with the refresh token rotating on each use. Keep it checked only if Composio refreshes GitHub tokens correctly in your test (see uncertainties). Otherwise uncheck it, and tokens will stay valid until revoked.

steps.title: Register, then generate a client secret
steps.detail: Click Register application. On the app page, click 'Generate a new client secret' and copy it right away, because it's shown only once. Copy the Client ID too. Upload a logo if you want one on the consent screen.

phases.title: Connect it in Composio and test with your own account
phases.goal: An OAuth flow finishes and API calls work with your account

steps.title: Create a custom auth config
steps.detail: Go to https://dashboard.composio.dev > Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > GitHub > OAuth2. Paste the Client ID and Client Secret. Set scopes, for example repo,user,gist,notifications,project,workflow,codespace or a smaller set. Click Create and copy the ac_... ID.

steps.title: Pass the auth config in your session
steps.detail: Pass authConfigs: { github: 'ac_...' } in the Composio session. Toolkits you don't list keep using managed auth.

steps.title: Run the connect flow
steps.detail: Authorize with your own GitHub account. The consent screen should show your app name and the scopes you requested. Then call GET https://api.github.com/user and read the X-OAuth-Scopes response header to see which scopes you actually got.

steps.title: Test org repos
steps.detail: List the repos of an org you belong to. If private org repos are missing, the org has OAuth app access restrictions turned on. Approve your app at Org Settings > Third-party Access > OAuth app policy, or ask an owner to.

phases.title: Go live
phases.goal: Any GitHub user can connect, and org customers know how to approve you
phases.waitTime: None from GitHub. Each org owner's approval takes whatever time they take.

steps.title: Ship without waiting for review
steps.detail: GitHub has no review or verification step for OAuth apps. The app is live for all users as soon as it's registered.

steps.title: Document org approval for customers
steps.detail: Explain to users how to request approval on the consent screen: there's a 'Request' button next to each org. Explain to org owners how to grant it under Settings > Third-party Access > OAuth app policy. For SAML SSO orgs, the user must also have an active SSO session when authorizing.

steps.title: Transfer the app to an org account if you created it under a personal account
steps.detail: On the app's settings page, use Transfer ownership. This keeps the app safe if an employee leaves.

phases.title: Ongoing maintenance
phases.goal: Tokens stay valid and secrets stay safe

steps.title: Rotate the client secret when needed
steps.detail: Generate a new secret, update the Composio auth config, then delete the old secret.

steps.title: Handle revocations and reconnects
steps.detail: Users can revoke the app or edit its scopes at any time. If expiring tokens are on and a refresh token goes unused for 6 months, GitHub returns bad_refresh_token and the user must reconnect. Too many re-auths can hit the 10-tokens-per-user/app/scope cap.

scopes.purpose: Full read/write access to public and private repos (code, issues, PRs, statuses, webhooks)
scopes.reviewNote: No GitHub review. This is very broad, and org owners and security-minded users may push back. Use public_repo if you only need public repos.

scopes.purpose: Read/write access to public repos only
Create and edit GitHub Actions workflow files
scopes.reviewNote: No review, but needed for any push that touches .github/workflows. Request it only if you need it.

blockers.title: Org OAuth app access restrictions
blockers.symptom: The user connects fine, but org private repos are missing from results, return 404, or the API says the org has restricted OAuth app access.
blockers.fix: The org owner approves the app under Org Settings > Third-party Access > OAuth app policy, or the user clicks 'Request' on the consent screen. Restrictions are on by default for new orgs.

blockers.title: SAML SSO-protected orgs
blockers.symptom: 403 with a message that resource access requires SAML enforcement or SSO authorization.
blockers.fix: The user signs in through their org's SSO and then re-authorizes, or authorizes the token for SSO. The org must also approve the app.

blockers.title: redirect_uri mismatch
blockers.symptom: GitHub shows 'The redirect_uri is not associated with this application' or returns error=redirect_uri_mismatch.
blockers.fix: Set the callback URL to exactly https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Apps created after Aug 3, 2026 use exact matching by default.

blockers.title: Expiring tokens and refresh rotation
blockers.symptom: Calls fail after 8 hours, or refresh returns bad_refresh_token.
blockers.fix: Make sure the refresh works through Composio. If it doesn't, uncheck 'Expire user access tokens' in the app settings and have users reconnect, since existing tokens don't change.

blockers.title: Token cap per user/app/scope
blockers.symptom: Older connections stop working after a user reconnects many times.
blockers.fix: GitHub keeps at most 10 tokens per user/app/scope combination. Reuse existing connections instead of re-authorizing.

blockers.title: Missing scope because the user edited it
blockers.symptom: 403 'Resource not accessible' even though you requested the scope.
blockers.fix: Check the X-OAuth-Scopes header and ask the user to reconnect with the needed scopes.

technical.pkce: Supported and recommended. S256 only, plain is not supported. code_challenge and code_challenge_method must be sent together.
technical.refreshTokens: Opt-in, but the 'Expire user access tokens' box is checked by default for new apps. With it on, access tokens last 8 hours (expires_in 28800) and refresh tokens expire after 6 months unused. Each refresh rotates both tokens and invalidates the old ones. Scopes can't change on refresh. With it off, tokens don't expire until revoked. Changing the setting doesn't affect tokens already issued. Authorization codes expire after 10 minutes.
technical.redirectUriRules: Up to 10 callback URLs. Exact match by default. Wildcard matching (subdomains and subpaths) can be turned on per callback URL. Apps that had a single callback before Aug 3, 2026 have wildcard matching on as legacy behavior. If redirect_uri is omitted, GitHub uses the first callback. For native apps, use 127.0.0.1 or ::1 loopback with any port.
technical.notes: No OIDC/RFC 8414 discovery metadata (tested). No implicit grant, and no CORS on the token endpoint. Send Accept: application/json to the token endpoint to get JSON back. OAuth apps use coarse scopes. GitHub recommends GitHub Apps for fine-grained permissions, but Composio's GitHub toolkit uses OAuth app scopes. GitHub Enterprise Server uses per-host URLs (https://HOST/login/oauth/...) and needs a separate app on that instance. Max 100 OAuth apps per owner.

To let [PRODUCT] work with your organization's private repositories, an owner of the [ORG_NAME] GitHub organization needs to approve our app:
1. Go to https://github.com/organizations/[ORG_NAME]/settings/oauth_application_policy
2. Find "[APP_NAME]" under pending requests, or ask a member to request access from the GitHub authorization screen.
3. Click Grant / Approve.
[PRODUCT] uses these scopes: [SCOPES]. We use them to [PURPOSE, e.g. read issues and open pull requests on your behalf]. Each user's access never exceeds their own GitHub permissions, and any user can revoke it at https://github.com/settings/applications.
